texts.preamble: Master Shaik Faisal @ Faisal vs M/S Voler Car Pvt. Ltd on 21 August, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru. (Scch-18) Dated: This 21st day of August 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.685/2018
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 29.3.2017 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was a pedestrian walking on the Kanakapura main road in front of Rajegowda Military hotel, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018 came from the opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner. Consequent to the terrific impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Sagar hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took the first aid treatment, thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS and then he was referred to Victoria hospital and again he was shifted to Chaya Medical Centre, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 14 years, studying in 7th standard at New Mother land School, Avalahalli, Bengaluur. On account of the injuries he could not attend the class and lost one academic year. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car. Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte. The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.2 in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that Master Shaik Faisal @ Faisal vs M/S Voler Car Pvt. Ltd on 21 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109505988/ 2 neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AF-8018 and its validity. Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident. Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 1. 7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P13 & Ex.P14. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has examined official of the RTO as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
texts.arguments: Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident. Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2. 13. 14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition. 16 . The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who while trying to cross the busy Kanakapura main road, where there is no provision for pedestrians to cross the said road and suddenly he came to the middle of the road and running negligently in a abrupt manner and caused the accident. To substantiate the said fact, he has not examined any witness or produced any documents to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner. On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 27. At this juncture this court has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 in between Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd.,and another, which reads like thus; Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Assessment of compensation in case of children suffering disability - Apex Court observed that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10 per cent and up to 30 per cent to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; up to 60 percent, Rs.4,00,000; up to 90 per cent, Rs.5,00,000 and above 90 per cent, it should be Rs.6,00,000; for permanent disability up to 10 per cent, it should be Rs.1,00,000, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick. 34. At this juncture this court has drawn the attention on the decision reported in 2017 ACJ 2011 in between Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., which reads thus; Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section3 and 10(2) (d) ---Driving licence---Light motor vehicle---whether a person holding driving licence to drive 'light motor vehicle' is competent to drive transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kgs or a motor car or tractor or road roller, the unladden weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kg---Held yes, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class; a licence issued under section 10(2) (d) continues to be valid after amendment vide Act 54 of 1994 in MV Act and in form 4 under rule 14 (1) of Central Motor vehicles Rules, 1989, w.e.f. 28.3.2001. 35.
